implementation_constraints: pure stdlib only (sys, json, re); reads entire stdin, prints one JSON array (decode) or one JSON array of frame strings (encode) to stdout, exits 0 even on ERROR
batch is atomic: first malformed frame/message aborts the whole decode/encode and prints exactly the literal text ERROR (no JSON) instead of partial output

frame validity check order: reject empty string, then require TYPE segment to fully match ^[A-Z]+$, then each subsequent segment must contain '=' with key matching ^[a-z]+$ and the extracted value containing no further '=' (multiple '=' in one segment is malformed, not swallowed into the value)

unresolved_intent.decision: a segment with more than one '=' (e.g. a=b=c) is treated as malformed, not as key='a', value='b=c'
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec states a value cannot contain '=' at all; splitting on the FIRST '=' then re-checking the tail for '=' enforces that literally rather than silently accepting it as part of the value

unresolved_intent.ir_region: decode input frame that is not a JSON string (e.g. number/null in the frames array)
unresolved_intent.decision: treated as a malformed frame, aborting the whole batch with ERROR, same as a structurally bad frame string
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec only defines frame validity for strings; any non-string array element can't have been produced by a legal encode, so it falls under 'malformed frame' rather than a separate top-level-shape error

unresolved_intent.ir_region: duplicate keys within one message/frame's field list
unresolved_intent.decision: duplicates are allowed and preserved as-is in order; no deduplication or last-wins merging
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec only requires ORDER to be preserved and never mentions key uniqueness, so inventing a dedup rule would be adding behavior not in the contract

unresolved_intent.decision: legal: type-only frames decode to fields: [] and encode back to just the type string with no trailing '|'
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec explicitly gives PING as an example of a valid frame with zero fields
